original_question: Let F: Ω → P_0(X) be a multifunction from a complete probability space into the nonempty subsets of a Banach space X. If F has convex closed values and is scalarly measurable, meaning F^{-}(H) is measurable for every open half-space H ⊆ X, must F admit a selector f: Ω → X that is itself scalarly measurable?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.7 in Section 2.3 (Measurable selectors): whether every scalarly measurable multi-function F: Ω → P0(X) with convex closed values has a scalarly measurable selector. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
correct_elements: You already captured almost all of the paper’s actual question: the complete probability-space setting, the Banach-space target, the multi-function F: Ω → P0(X), the convex closed value hypothesis, the half-space formulation of scalar measurability for F, and the desired conclusion that there should exist a selector that is itself scalarly measurable. This is essentially Problem 2.7. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper writes the ambient measure space explicitly as a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ), so the σ-algebra Σ with respect to which all measurability is taken should be named. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, define P0(X) explicitly as the family of all non-empty subsets of X. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

The selector condition should be stated explicitly: a selector is a map f: Ω → X such that f(t) ∈ F(t) for every t ∈ Ω. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

If the notation F^{-}(H) is used, it should be defined as F^{-}(G) := {t ∈ Ω : F(t) ∩ G ≠ ∅}; the paper introduces this notation immediately before defining scalar measurability. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

To match the paper exactly, note the global convention that all Banach spaces under consideration are real Banach spaces. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

For the selector’s measurability, the paper spells out that scalar measurability means x*∘f is Σ-measurable for every x* ∈ X*. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let (Ω, Σ, μ) be a complete probability space, let X be a real Banach space, and let P0(X) denote the family of all non-empty subsets of X. Suppose F: Ω → P0(X) is a multi-function with convex closed values such that F^{-}(H) := {t ∈ Ω : F(t) ∩ H ≠ ∅} belongs to Σ for every open half-space H ⊆ X. Must there exist a selector f: Ω → X, meaning f(t) ∈ F(t) for every t ∈ Ω, such that x*∘f is Σ-measurable for every x* ∈ X*? ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: under the same hypotheses, must F admit a selector f: Ω → X that is measurable with respect to the Baire σ-algebra Ba(X,w) of X endowed with its weak topology? The paper states that for single-valued maps f, scalar measurability is equivalent to Ba(X,w)-measurability. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
justification: The draft is a near-verbatim capture of the paper’s actual target and should be aligned with Problem 2.7, not with the neighboring Problems 2.8 or 2.9. Those later questions concern property (SC) for the families wk(X) and cwk(X), whereas your draft asks directly about one scalarly measurable multi-function with convex closed values. The immediately surrounding text on the same page provides the exact notation P0(X), the definition of selector, the inverse-image notation F^{-}(G), the definition of scalar measurability for multi-functions, the equivalence between scalar measurability and Ba(X,w)-measurability for single-valued maps, and the motivating known positive result when the values are weakly compact. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
